1. Approach and Rationale:
    Our primary approach leverages an alternating optimization paradigm inspired by autoregressive modeling and impulse response representation. We represent the coefficients as an impulse train combined with optimization of high-pass gain profiles. The method:
    (a) Starts from parent initialization or uniform random initialization
    (b) Represents tentative solutions as sparse impulse patterns
    (c) Reinforces mass toward optimal autocorrelation locality
    (d) Iteratively refines concentration while bounding the AC1 magnitude
    Our approach differs fundamentally from the parent program by direct impulse optimization rather than gradient-based continuous space navigation.

 2. Mathematical Specification:
    We optimize sequence a of length n with:
    - Nonnegativity constraints: a_i ≥ 0 ∀i
    - Sum constraint: ∑a_i ≥ 0.01
    The objective is to find a that minimizes:
        AC1 = 2n * max_{k}(∑_{i} a_i a_{k-i}) / (∑a)^2
    Our method uses:
        • Linear interpolation between candidate bases
        • Autocorrelation locality measurement as fitness metric
        • Convexity within local optimization regions
    The core mathematical innovation is the decomposition into:
        S(k) = ∑_{i} a_i a_{k-i} = ⟨a, τ^k a⟩
    Where τ is the shift operator.

 3. Implementation Procedure:
    a) Orchestration:
        i. Initialize from parent sequence (if available) or uniform random
        ii. Set adaptive parameters (anneal_rate=0.95, base_prune=0.8)
        iii. Begin iterative refinement
    b) Candidate generation:
        i. Maintenance transform: Map a to autocorrelation spectrum C
        ii. High-magnitude impulse training
        iii. Balanced local refinement
    c) Objective evaluation:
        i. Full convolution via explicit summation (no FFT)
        ii. Select maximum correlation value
    d) Optimization loop:
        1. Local concentration: Apply entropy pruning
        2. Global optimization: Sweep autocorrelation map
        3. Boundary adjustment: Taper tails to zero

 4. Search Choices and Variations:
    a) Optimization Start:
        • "balance": Balanced impulse distribution
        • "local": High-frequency modes first (used mainly as restart)
    b) Objective Correction:
        • "prune": Remove low-impact components (default if plateau)
        • "power": Reinforce high-magnitude modes (default on annealing)
        • "bound": Maintain autocorrelation bounds (final state method)
    c) Segmentation Size:
        • S = n//4 (default) (integer)
        • S = n//8 for stability
        • S = n//2 for efficiency

 5. Compute Budget and Robustness:
    a) Dominant costs:
        o Convolution: O(n^2) per evaluation
        o Segment management: O(n)
        o Local optimizations: O(n log n)
    b) Deadline adaptation:
        • Start with 100 full evaluations
        • Use piecewise timeout: 90%, 95%, 99%
        • Fallback to strongest impulse solution
    c) Stability:
        • Each solution prunes no more than 10% per step
        • Minimum component count maintained
        • Explicit zero-checking before evaluation

 6. Validation and Return Contract:
    a) Candidate checks for:
        i. Finite, nonnegative values
        ii. Convolution max defined
        iii. Sum >=0.01
    b) Explicit scoring call:
        score = evaluate_sequence(candidate_vector)
    c) Metric reporting:
        Lower score bound = target AC1 value
        Current best evaluated
        Broken: Fails normalization
    d) Final fallback:
        return [1000.0/n for _ in range(n)]
